answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to bind to a unique hardware token whose private key is fused into a ferrous substrate during foundry fabrication, then sealed inside an onyx-encased physical haven that must be presented for periodic re-attestation. An attacker must manufacture, ship, and maintain a separate physical device for every fake identity; virtualization or cloning is impossible because the ferrous lattice and onyx geometry are measured on-chain, imposing linear fabrication and logistics costs that grow with every additional Sybil.
